details: UCOP FY2025: US$5.970892 billion held by the Regents for Berkeley; US$3.379223 billion in Foundation assets outside Regents pools; US$0.014953 billion in Foundation short-term pool investments. The components sum to US$9.365068 billion, without double counting.

details: This is explicitly cash assets of named trusts/estates, not the university’s consolidated permanent investment corpus.
The separate Stiftung Humboldt-Universität supports HU and accepts gifts to permanent capital; its assets must not be assumed to be included in this cash table.
The Alexander von Humboldt Foundation is a separate national research-support organization and must not be used as HU’s endowment.

The Gerd Rodenwaldt trust assets are shown in Free Berlin’s budget; HU receives half of annual interest under an agreement. Do not add half of those principal assets to HU or double-count across institutions.
The official budget index currently requires login and direct downloads return a challenge. No 2026 budget or 2024 actual trust-capital total could be independently verified.

reading.title: Scale is only part of the story
reading.text: Harvard’s reported endowment is far larger than the other U.S. cases. Restrictions, annual distributions, and funding commitments determine how much of that capital can support a new choice.

reading.title: A financial history needs definitions
reading.text: Berkeley’s broader reporting scope, Harvard’s deferred tax provision, and differing pledge and trust treatment affect comparisons. Read the dated values as reported balances, rather than a single measure of investment performance.
